quotes.text:
Art can help us see the world differently and to understand each other better! Thank you to all the participants of the #IL03's 2024 Congressional Art Competition. Your art is an inspiration and a representation of the diversity and talent of our district. Big congrats to our winners!

🥇: "My Gift to AI" by Emma Jack 
🥈: “Brave” by Pedro Morales
🥉: “Rainy Days” by Mildred Vargas

Their big horrible bill is packed full of the worst sneak attacks - from going after civil society organizations to forbidding regulation of AI.

The bill both robs our communities of resources and tries to undermine our ability to fight back against authoritarianism, human rights abuses, and the erosion of democratic freedoms. 

The nonprofit killer clause may be gone, but the bill is still a big HELL NO for me.

The bigotry and racism coming from the White House is deplorable. 

From AI videos to mass detention of immigrant families to the threats of disfranchising Black and Brown voters, the Trump Administration has made white supremacy their policy. It is morally bankrupt. It is harmful. It is unacceptable. They will be held accountable.

Are you, the small government people, suggesting that the government surveilled and created a list using AI of people exercising their right to dissent?

Like fascist, authoritarian governments do? https://t.co/jEnEVBp0P1

AI tools are being used to surveil, target, and violate our rights and privacy.
 
We cannot settle for unregulated, unaccountable AI. We must establish rules, limits, and oversight on AI companies. https://t.co/rauTkkSL2t

This whole move fast and break things is not acceptable innovation strategy when we know that the things that end up being broken are not just a computer, a laptop, a cell phone. It’s people’s lives, their rights and their privacy.
And I have had a front row seat as the Trump administration has aggressively accelerated the use of technology and artificial intelligence in its militarized immigration enforcement campaign.

When the government can quietly collect enormous amounts of personal information, analyze it with artificial intelligence and make decisions with limited transparency or accountability, ALL of our rights and liberties are at risk.

As AI continues to be recklessly accelerated by big tech, we are witnessing how dangerously powerful it can be without guardrails, oversight, or accountability.

AI poses real risks to infrastructure, journalists, advocates, professors, lawyers, and students.

That’s why Congressional action to ensure the people have oversight and to regulate AI is so essential to protecting our privacy, civil liberties, and democratic institutions.

The incident raises a number of serious questions regarding the rigor with which OpenAI secures and monitors its testing environments and the tools used to support them. [...] Safety, security, and innovation must coexist.

Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people. [...] At the same time, Artificial Intelligence threatens to displace millions of American workers. [...] Unfortunately, Congress has so far completely failed to respond to the threats posed by AI development. That must change.

Employees are sounding the alarms: Big Tech doesn't care about protecting us from AI as long as they profit. 
 
AI tools are being recklessly accelerated by big tech without guardrails, oversight, or accountability.
 
We must demand Congressional oversight and action to protect our privacy, civil liberties, and democratic institutions from the dangers of AI.

Letting the foxes guard the chicken coop HAS NEVER BEEN good policy. Every single time, our communities suffer.

But Trump and Johnson don't care about the pain they inflict on us as long as they profit.

We cannot settle for unregulated, unaccountable AI. Congress has the obligation to demand rules and limits, pass legislation, and conduct oversight of AI companies.

My district is demanding more than a bill that suggests states take action. Congress must demand rules and limits, pass legislation that protects people, and conduct oversight of AI companies and data centers. Anything else doesn’t meet the moment.

Yesterday, you heard me say we need oversight of AI. Well, today, I joined @RepJayapal for a shadow hearing on AI. 
 
Investors are betting trillions of dollars on AI for one purpose: the possibility that it will someday replace humans… replace workers. But let’s be clear: AI needs US. WE do not need AI.
 
Working people need to be in the driver’s seat. We, the people, can decide rules and limits, civil rights and protections, and proper oversight and guardrails for AI.

Instead of working to address the harms of AI, Johnson cancelled the remaining votes this month.   You and I know that, despite what Trump and Johnson say, AI companies can’t and won’t regulate themselves.   Congress must act to protect the American people’s privacy, safety, and civil liberties.

Investors are betting trillions of dollars on AI for one purpose: the possibility that it will someday replace humans… replace workers. But let’s be clear: AI needs US. WE do not need AI.

We won't let diversions, rebrands, misdirection, or fake corporate "accords" confuse or deter us. We will not leave it to Trump and corporate CEOs to keep us safe - they won't and they never have.

We, the people, can decide rules and limits, civil rights and protections, and proper oversight and guardrails for AI.

EVERY worker deserves living wages, safe working conditions, fair benefits, and, as AI continues to be recklessly accelerated by big tech, guaranteed protections against AI.

I stand with the Cook County College Teachers Union and every worker demanding a fair contract.

I call on all parties to come to the table and negotiate in good faith-- centering workers and students, not profit.

As AI continues to be recklessly accelerated, I joined @ConMijente, organizers, movement leaders, researchers, and public officials to discuss how we protect our communities from unregulated, unaccountable tech. 
 
Working people need to be in the driver’s seat! We, the people, can decide rules and limits, civil rights and protections, and proper oversight and guardrails for AI.
 
This is the moment to keep organizing, mobilizing, and amplifying!

Everyday makes it clearer: Congress can't allow AI to continue operate without guardrails, oversight, or accountability.

The reckless acceleration of AI has shown us that it can be a threat to working families and our democracy.

But we don't need AI; it needs us. We must take action to protect our privacy, civil liberties, and democratic institutions.
